clue.text: Round of beef?

parts.note: a round of beef is normally a cut of the leg, but read literally it is a ball-shaped piece of minced beef

explanation.definitionFit: A ball of minced beef is literally a round thing made of beef.

clue.text: Fashionable, sixties-style?

parts.note: mods were a 1960s British youth culture of sharp suits and scooters
-ish is a suffix meaning in the style of

explanation.surface: Something trendy in a 1960s way.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were the stylish 1960s British youth movement; the suffix -ISH means somewhat like.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means in the current fashion, stylish.

clue.text: Promise to show ship in a river

indicators.note: in places the ship inside the other pieces

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone vows to display a ship on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure someone is to promise or guarantee them something.

clue.text: Live with desire to become socially acceptable

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live
to long is to desire

explanation.surface: Living with ambition in order to fit into society.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong is to fit in and be accepted by a group.

clue.text: Be highly patronising?

parts.note: being condescending is pictured literally as gazing from a height at people

explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone with contempt, regarding them as beneath you.

clue.text: Work on model counter

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone sets to work on a model counter, a shop fitting or a scale model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb: to counter is to oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter an argument or plan is to resist it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hesitation in cutting power lines proves wrong-headed

indicators.note: in cutting says the hesitation slices into the power and lines

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
verse is lines of poetry
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Dithering over cutting power cables proves stubbornly misguided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power lines' reads as electric cables; it is P plus VERSE, cut by ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary, obstinately unreasonable.

clue.text: More than achieve object, but exhaust oneself

parts.note: to overdo is to do more than needed
it is an object pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone exceeds their goal but wears themselves out.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo it is idiom for working too hard and tiring yourself.

clue.text: Being put out about the whole effect

indicators.note: put out says the being is stretched open to take in another piece

parts.note: an entity is a being
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed about the overall impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as 'annoyed' in the surface, but it signals the word for 'Being' opened up to take in the short word for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety means the whole of something, complete totality.

clue.text: Ban detective with unhealthy complexion

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
a sallow face is yellowish and sickly

explanation.surface: A pale, sickly detective is barred from something.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow a goal or claim is to rule it out, a synonym of forbid.

clue.text: Keen to be part of vineyard enterprise

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to join a wine-making business.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Keen to be' as the definition, but 'to be' cannot stand in for the answer; it is the link joining 'Keen' to the hidden-word signal 'part of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionately eager, a synonym of keen.

clue.text: Song composed about Bill

indicators.note: about tells us the calm word goes around the bill

parts.note: composed means calm, serene
AD is short for advertisement, a bill or poster

explanation.surface: A song has been written concerning a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like an anagram signal, but here it means calm; 'about' wraps that calm word round the short form of an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song sung under a window.

clue.text: Drinking bout gets you brightly coloured nose on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the two pieces together are read backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: red is a bright colour
neb is a dialect word for a beak or nose

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker ends up with a red nose, noticed on thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns REDNEB round as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is slang for a long spell of heavy drinking.

clue.text: Dessert topping you'll see English and carry about

annotationWithheld.why: 'Dessert topping you'll see English and carry about' (5,5): the anagram needs MAID beside E and CARRY, and no clue word gives MAID; the clue seems cut or garbled and no scan or reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dessert topping you'll see English and carry about

clue.text: Saw the stir created by fashion garment

indicators.note: created signals the letters of the three words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone sees the fuss a fashion item causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created by' reads as the cause of the stir; 'created' is the anagram signal on SAW THE STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatshirt is a loose cotton top, an item of casual clothing.

clue.text: Novel sort of raincoat

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A new kind of waterproof coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective, 'new'; it is the noun, Stevenson's sequel to Kidnapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Catriona is a book by Robert Louis Stevenson, published 1893.

clue.text: Perennial student?

parts.note: a perpetual student is suggested, but the perennials are plants and the student studies them

explanation.definitionFit: A plant scientist studies perennials among other flora.

clue.text: Indian region abandoned by doctor

indicators.note: abandoned suggests the letters of region are thrown about wildly

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer

explanation.surface: A doctor leaves an Indian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' reads as 'left by'; 'abandoned' alone is the anagram signal, and 'by' just joins the doctor on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was an Apache leader, a Native American.

clue.text: Openly describing MD's position?

explanation.definitionFit: Done openly, without deceit; and a managing director sits over the board of directors.

clue.text: Go off royal painter

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: A court artist departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal painter' reads as a court artist; J. M. W. Turner was the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. W. Turner was the great English landscape artist.

clue.text: No problem accepting the thing's restricted

indicators.note: accepting says the okay word takes the thing in

parts.note: fine means okay, no problem
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: The thing is limited, which is no problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Finite means having limits, bounded.

clue.text: Still puts key questions about ringleader

parts.note: A is a musical key

indicators.note: about says the test goes round the leader

parts.note: a test is a set of questions
the leader, or first letter, of ring

explanation.surface: Someone asks crucial questions about the gang boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' reads as the gang boss; it gives R, the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: At rest means motionless, not moving.

clue.text: Argue capital offence must be initially ignored

indicators.note: initially ignored says the first letter is dropped from the crime

parts.note: treason was a crime punishable by death

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a hanging offence should be disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone is to argue or persuade logically.

clue.text: Make familiar with account that's curious

parts.note: quaint means odd, curious

explanation.surface: A banker gets to know a client's odd account.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with a fact is to inform them of it.

clue.text: Start by bringing benefit cheque back home

indicators.note: back says the cheque word is read in reverse

parts.note: a giro was the cheque in which British welfare benefit was paid
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone begins by bringing their welfare cheque back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GIRO into ORIG; GIRO is the British unemployment-benefit cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the beginning or source of something.

clue.text: Close season just now

parts.note: close means stingy, mean
a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: The closed season for hunting is currently in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close season' reads as a sporting term; 'Close' means tight-fisted, MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In the meantime means for now, during the interval.

clue.text: Fighting gesture

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers see action in combat; and an action is a movement or gesture.

clue.text: Issue related to conservation body is coming out

parts.note: to issue is to come forth, emerge
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A matter connected with a conservation group is being made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a noun but works as the verb. The National Trust looks after historic British houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emergent is arising or appearing, newly coming into view.
